- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% for next 3–5 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% for the following 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.3) mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust downward; reduce forecast by 3–8% for next 3–7 days.  
- Model frequently overestimates mean reversion speed; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, forecast should be slightly below 30-day moving average for next 5–10 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overpredict late-period prices (last 7–10 days); cap forecast at 10% below true outcome for final 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; adjust forecast to match sentiment trend direction for next 3–5 days.
